title: Setup Guide
text:
IDE
Install and use an IDE of your choice, preferably Zed or VSCode.

Zed

Zed is a fast, open-source editor with a built-in AI agent, so you don’t need to install any extension to get coding assistance. We will use it during the school together with the API key you will be given, see Agent Integration below.


WindowsmacOSLinux


Download the installer from the download page, or run in PowerShell:
winget install -e --id ZedIndustries.Zed


Download from the download page, or run in Terminal:
curl -f https://zed.dev/install.sh | sh


Run in a terminal:
curl -f https://zed.dev/install.sh | sh
Your distribution may also package Zed, in which case feel free to use your package manager.



Zed keeps itself up to date, so you only need to do this once.

title: Setup Guide
text:
Agent Integration

During the school you will be granted access to LLM Agent via OpenRouter to support you in coding. OpenRouter is a gateway that gives you access to many models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, open-weight models, …) through a single API key – the one you will receive at the start of the school.







Note



If you already use a different coding assistant or have a Claude subscription, you can use your own settings, we do not require you to use this.



Add your API key to Zed

Zed settings UIEnvironment variable


This is the recommended way – the key is stored in your system keychain and survives restarts.

Open the settings from the menu: Zed > Open Settings (ctrl-,, on macOS cmd-,).

Pick AI in the left sidebar, and under General click Configure next to LLM Providers.

Scroll down to the OpenRouter section and paste the key you were given into the API Key field, then confirm with enter.


Once the key is accepted, OpenRouter models show up in the model selector in the agent panel.


Instead of pasting the key into the settings, you can set the OPENROUTER_API_KEY environment variable – Zed reads it from the environment it was started in, so you have to restart Zed for it to take effect.

WindowsmacOSLinux


setx OPENROUTER_API_KEY "sk-or-v1-REPLACE-ME"
setx stores the variable permanently, but it only applies to programs started after you run it.


export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-or-v1-REPLACE-ME"
This is not permanent – it only applies to the current terminal session, so start Zed from that same terminal (zed .), or add the line to your ~/.zshrc.


export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-or-v1-REPLACE-ME"
This is not permanent – it only applies to the current terminal session, so start Zed from that same terminal (zed .), or add the line to your ~/.bashrc.








Using the agent in Zed

Agent panel – click the ✨ icon in the status bar, or run agent: new thread from the command palette. This is the chat-style assistant that can read and edit files in your project.
Pick a model – use the model selector above the message box, or cmd-alt-/ (macOS) / ctrl-alt-/ (Windows/Linux). With the school key, only GLM 5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash are available.
Inline assist – press ctrl-enter in the editor or terminal to ask for a change right where your cursor is; select a block of code first to have it rewritten.







Tip



If you want to set a default model, so you don’t have to pick it in every new thread, you can edit Zed’s settings.json directly – Zed > Open Settings File (ctrl-alt-,, on macOS cmd-alt-,):
{
  "agent": {
    "default_model": {
      "provider": "openrouter",
      "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"
    }
  }
}
The other available model is GLM 5.3 Flash – you can copy its exact identifier from the model selector or from the OpenRouter models page.








ImportantAttention




Never share your key or commit it to a repository.
The key is time-limited, has a spending limit, and will stop working after the school.
Only two models are available to you: GLM 5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.
Never put personal data or non-public information into the agent – whatever you send goes to a third-party service.

title: Training school programme
text:
Case Studies
Throughout the school, participants will work with four real-world archaeological datasets:

Artefact types: classification and detection of archaeological artefacts from photographs
Microscopic use-wear analysis: identifying and classifying wear traces from microscopic images
Satellite imagery: remote sensing and object detection on satellite data
Rock art:
Coins: combining techniques on photographs and drawings of coins and exploring model interpretability

title: Applications
text:
Who should apply

We welcome applications from early-career researchers and students who are enthusiastic about exploring the potential of computer vision and machine learning in archaeological research. This school will focus on the practical application of image analysis techniques to archaeological image data, from dataset preparation and model training to evaluation and emerging methods such as vision-language models.
While applicants with prior experience in Python and/or machine learning are encouraged to apply, the first day of the training will be dedicated to the fundamentals of Python for image analysis tasks. Participants should have basic experience with any programming or markup language (e.g. HTML, R, Python or similar) and a general comfort with working in digital environments. No prior experience with Python or machine learning is strictly required, but curiosity and a willingness to engage with technical material are essential.

title: About the training school
text:
Organisations

ATRIUM

The training school is organised as transnational access provision in the ATRIUM Project (Advancing Frontier Research in the Arts and Humanities) funded by the Horizon Europe research and innovation actions programme under grant agreement No. 101132163. ATRIUM project covers the organizational costs of the school and participator grants.




MAIA

MAIA (Managing Artificial Intelligence in Archaeology) is a COST Action (CA23141) funded by the European Union co-organizing the training school. MAIA COST Action covers travel and subsistence costs of two MAIA instructors.




AIS CR

The Archaeological Information System of the Czech Republic (AIS CR) is a research infrastructure integrating digital resources and services on archaeology in the Czech Republic, and as such is one of many data providers in the ARIADNE Research Infrastructure. AIS CR is jointly operated by the Institutes of Archaeology of the Czech Academy of Sciences in Brno (IAB) and Prague (IAP). AIS CR/IAB provides the infrastructure and the venue for the training school.

title: Computer Vision in Archaeology
text:
NoteBasics



When? 14–18 September 2026
Where? Brno, Czech Republic
What? Training school on computer vision and machine learning in archaeology








ImportantPre-school survey



If you are among selected participants, please fill in a pre-school survey here.



Join us for an intensive one-week training school dedicated to computer vision in archaeology, where you will learn how to harness the power of modern machine learning techniques to detect, classify, and analyse archaeological features and artefacts in images. As visual data — from drone surveys and excavation photography to museum collections — continues to grow in volume, the ability to process and interpret it computationally is becoming an increasingly valuable skill in the archaeologist’s toolkit. Our programme guides you from the very foundations of Python programming through to hands-on experience with state-of-the-art object detection and image segmentation models, with dedicated sessions on dataset creation, model training, and evaluation. Participants should have basic experience with any programming or markup language and a general comfort with working in digital environments. No prior experience with machine learning is required, but curiosity and a willingness to engage with technical material are essential.






















The training school is part of a trans-national access scheme provided by the ATRIUM Project, hosted by the Archaeological Information System of the Czech Republic (AIS CR) research infrastructure at the Institute of Archaeology, Czech Academy of Sciences, Brno. The school is co-organized by the MAIA COST Action project. MAIA provides funding to several of the school instructors.
To apply and learn more about the TNA, visit the ATRIUM TNA Application website.

title: General Information
text:
Grants
Each participant of the school is eligible to receive a grant to cover travel expenses, housing, and daily subsistence during the meeting. To receive the grant, participants need to:

Apply via the official form of the ATRIUM Project (see the Applications section for details).
Participate in person, i.e. sign attendance sheets for each training day.
Submit a report within a given time frame after the conclusion of the school with details of their participation. Please note that the grant will be disbursed only upon the successful submission of this report.
